title.narrative: GEN - Empowering Women for Economic and Political Leadership in Guinea-Bissau

description.narrative: This project to strengthen inclusive governance and democratic resilience in Guinea-Bissau by empowering women and young women to participate actively in public life while also advancing their economic independence. It combines leadership development, institutional support, and advocacy with targeted interventions to improve women’s livelihoods, recognizing that economic empowerment and political participation are mutually reinforcing.

title.narrative: Women and young women (including women and girls with disabilities) gain leadership, planning, digital and financial skills to influence public life and lead community or institutional initiatives.

description.narrative:
1.1 Establish a Women’s Leadership Fellowship (two cycles, 25 participants each) combining: 1.1.1 Modular training on leadership, public speaking, advocacy, strategic planning, and financial and digital literacy, with a focus on emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. 1.1.2 Mentorship by women leaders from politics, public administration, and the private sector. 1.1.3 Mini-grants ($ 2,000–3,000) for small civic or community projects advancing gender equality or public participation.
1.2 Partner with a local institution (e.g. Escola Nacional de Administração, Academia de Liderança) to host and accredit the fellowship modules. 1.3 Facilitate participation in regional and online capacity-building opportunities (e.g. UNITAR courses, internships, and staff exchanges with peer organizations across the West Africa sub-region).
1.4 Pilot community savings and digital finance mechanisms (e.g. Village Savings and Loan Associations or Orange Money wallets) to promote financial inclusion and resilience among fellows. 1.5 Develop a digital peer network (WhatsApp / Facebook groups and basic e-learning content) managed by a women’s association for continued mentoring and collaboration.

title.narrative: Strengthened Livelihoods of Women Micro Entrepreneurs.

description.narrative: 2.1 Number of women vendors and traders accessing small grants and microcredit. 2.2 Number of trading spaces improved (sanitation, storage facilities). 2.3 % increase in income among participating women vendors.

title.narrative: Advocacy and Social Norm Change for Gender Equality: Discriminatory gender norms and narratives that restrict women's leadership are reduced, civic and public support for women's political participation is strengthened.

description.narrative: 3.1 Number of community dialogues held engaging men, youth, and traditional leaders. 3.2 Reach of "Women Lead" national campaign (radio, theatre, social media). 3.3 Number of participants in Annual Women's Leadership Forum and Award.
